verification: mocked: CI fixture HTTP through the FastAPI test client against fixture SQLite graphs with a fixture semantic source; the cache, key, invalidation and retrieval are the production modules.
interfaces: app.context_cache: ContextCache, Key, negative, digest, enabled

state.observed: Every pull request check passes on the tested commit.
state.accepted: The SV2-CTX-04 cases pass in the full brain-api suite on three Python versions; the SV2-CTX-01 to 03 context tests pass unchanged.
state.externally_verified: None; mocked fixture evidence only. G6 rollout must validate deployed behavior.

red.outcome: failure in CI on 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12: ModuleNotFoundError app.context_cache, no context.cache and no cache field in the response

compatibility: Against the SV2-CTX-03 response every field is unchanged; a ranked response gains a top level cache object and stats gain context_cache. Exact replays keep the SV2-CTX-01 operation semantics.
rollback_rehearsal: BRAIN_CONTEXT_CACHE=false keeps bounded per-request retrieval with cache.state disabled (test_disabled_caching_keeps_bounded_per_request_retrieval). The cache holds copies of retrieval results only; no authoritative object is written or deleted by caching or its rollback. Running the context request in a threadpool is request dispatch, not caching, and stays on under the rollback.
limitations: The cache is per process; separate brain-api replicas do not share entries.
The knowledge revision is the SQLite data_version of the graph file, so any graph write clears every entry, not only the affected project.
Grants load at process start; the in-process revocation path is exercised by changing the loaded grants.
Optional semantic and heat sources are not part of the knowledge revision; positive entries expire after thirty seconds and reduced results after two.
